changelog: Web UI tunnel, Braiins OS dashboard: empty Hashboards and 'Tunnel Error — Miner did not respond in time' on GetHashboards / Subscribe / SubscribeMetrics / SubscribeTemperatures / graphql. Braiins OS keeps some of its page's gRPC calls open for as long as the page is; the agent waited for them to finish (they never do), and each waiting call held one of the three places in that miner's queue, so the page's ordinary calls timed out behind them. gRPC calls are now answered piece by piece (webui_stream_head / _data / _end) on a connection of their own, the queue place is given back as soon as the answer starts, the call is closed when the browser closes the page (webui_stream_cancel) or the server connection drops, after 5 minutes without data, and at most 60 are open per farm PC. Needs the server update of the same day; with an older server nothing changes.

Web UI tunnel, faster pages: text replies (scripts, styles, pages, readings) over 1 KB are packed with gzip before they travel to the server, when the server says it can unpack them (accept_gzip) — about a quarter of the size on the farm's uplink. Pictures and fonts are sent as before. With an older server nothing changes.

Web UI tunnel: 'Miner did not respond in time'. When a miner gave no answer within 8 s on a connection the agent had kept open (the miner had rebooted or dropped it), the page failed at once. The agent now asks once more on a new connection first, logs which miner and file got no answer, and no longer handles the same timeout twice.

Web UI tunnel, Braiins OS: the dashboard showed 'Miner info: missing trailer' and an empty Hashboards list. Braiins OS pages talk to the miner with gRPC-web; when the miner puts the call's end-of-reply status (grpc-status / grpc-message) in HTTP trailers instead of in the reply body, the agent used to drop it. Those trailers are now passed on to the server, and gRPC requests are sent with 'TE: trailers' so the miner is allowed to send them. Other miners are unchanged.

Web UI tunnel: open miners whose web server resets our request (seen on AvalonMiner: 'Cannot reach miner (ECONNRESET): read ECONNRESET' on every try). Every request now carries a browser User-Agent; if a miner still resets the connection after the usual fresh-connection retries, the request is repeated the way a browser sends it (without the agent's own root/root login header) and then over HTTPS on port 443 (self-signed certificates accepted). The style that works is remembered per miner so later files go straight there, and the agent log says what it learnt. When nothing answers, the error lists what was tried. Antminer / Braiins behaviour is unchanged.

Polling gap is confirmed and self-healing. The agent now reports the gap it is using in every heartbeat (and at once when it changes), so the server can see a farm that missed the setting and send it again; and it polls once immediately after the gap changes, so the farm card shows the new gap straight away instead of after the first (possibly long) gap has passed.

Polling gap set in the app. The time between two polls of the machines is now chosen in Remote Access (Poll every 30 s / 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 min), one setting for all farms: the server sends it when the agent connects (welcome.poll_sec) and whenever it is changed (set_poll), the running poll timer is restarted with the new gap straight away, and the value is kept in .farm.json so an agent restart uses it at once. Until one is set in the app the agent keeps POLL_MS from .env, else 30 s. Each poll report now includes the gap in use (poll_stats.poll_sec), shown on the farm card. The heartbeat to the server is separate and unchanged, so a farm stays online between polls.

Log check support: when the backend fetches a miner's log after its last automatic restart, the agent now also sends the miner's fan speeds (RPM per fan) and chips found per hashboard, read from /cgi-bin/stats.cgi (fan[], chain[].asic_num, eeprom_loaded) or the cgminer 'stats' command (fanN, chain_acnN). The backend uses them to write messages like 'Fan 2 = 0 RPM — change fan 2' or 'Chain 1 = 55 chips detected (other chains 76) — check hashboard' next to the log in Telegram. Only when asked (with_snapshot); the manual Download Logs is unchanged.

Re-release of v1.1.43 (same code) so every PC updates: v1.1.43 hadn't reached the farm PCs. Includes the IP-range fixes (networks bigger than /24 and continuous ranges across networks polled in full; the farm's machine networks polled automatically; poll report shown per farm in Remote Access).

Fix machines on a farm's second network showing offline. IP ranges were cut short: a network bigger than /24 (10.0.0.0/23, /22) was only polled for its first 254 addresses, and a continuous range such as 192.168.70.1-192.168.73.254 only covered its first network (the end address was read as just its last number). Ranges now cover everything up to 4,096 addresses each, and also accept 192.168.70-73.* for several whole networks; overlapping ranges are polled once. Unless ranges are set in the app, the agent now polls LOCAL_SUBNET plus every network the farm's machines are on (sent by the server, refreshed every 5 minutes), so a farm spread over several networks is never half-polled; with neither, the PC's own networks. Polling knocks on 128 addresses at a time before reading the machines that answer 25 at a time, so more networks don't stretch the cycle. After each cycle the agent reports what it polled (ranges, where they came from, addresses, cycle time, machines found) — shown per farm in Remote Access.

Farms are chosen in the app, not in .env. The agent now identifies the PC (permanent id from the Windows MachineGuid + PC name, sent as x-agent-pc-id) and the server decides which farm it runs; a PC it has never seen waits under Remote Access → New agents until someone picks a farm or types a new farm name, and polls nothing meanwhile. PCs set up the old way (FARM_ID in .env) are linked to that farm automatically the first time. The farm and the IP ranges set in the app are kept in .farm.json so a restart knows them at once. No .env is needed any more: IP ranges come from the app (Remote Access → IP Ranges, now actually pushed to the agent), else LOCAL_SUBNET in .env, else the PC's own network cards (virtual/VPN adapters skipped, anything wider than /24 narrowed to the PC's /24). Handles new server messages pending / assigned / farm_renamed / set_subnets, and reconnects at once (code 4010) when its farm is changed in the app. Polling starts on the server's welcome instead of on connect.

One agent per PC, enforced PC-wide (new agent-guard.js). The old guard was a lock file in the agent's own folder, so a second copy in another folder never saw it, and START.bat opened while PM2 already ran the updater started a second updater that restarted its refused agent forever while both rewrote the agent files. Now the running updater and agent each hold a loopback port (127.0.0.1:47811 / 47812): any second copy, from any folder, is refused with the farm, folder and process that is already running; Windows frees the port the moment a process dies, so a crash never leaves a stale lock. A refused agent under an updater exits with code 3 and the updater checks again every minute (no restart loop, message shown once); a refused copy under PM2 stands by and takes over if the other stops. If the port is used by an unrelated program the old folder lock is used instead. 'node agent-guard.js --status' shows what runs; '--stop-others' (used by SETUP-WINDOWS.bat) stops every other Ekalavya agent on the PC.

Fix Braiins OS 26.x showing 'Miner info: missing trailer' and empty Hardware Information / Hashboards through the web UI tunnel. Its dashboard calls the miner's gRPC-web API (GetMinerDetails, GetHashboards, GetMetadata…) with binary protobuf bodies; those bodies are now forwarded as raw bytes (base64 over the agent link, body_encoding) instead of being lost, the reply's grpc-status / grpc-message headers are returned (a call's result lives there when the reply has no body — dropping them is what the browser reported as 'missing trailer'), x-grpc-web / x-user-agent / grpc-timeout are passed to the miner, and the agent's root/root Basic header is no longer added to gRPC calls (gRPC reads Authorization as its own login token, so ours looked like an invalid token).

Relay live WebSockets from a miner's web UI through the tunnel. Braiins OS 26.x streams its whole dashboard (hashrate, chip temperature, fans, hashboards, pools) over a GraphQL WebSocket at /graphql; the backend refused every socket under /api/webui/, so the page logged in and drew its layout but every panel spun forever ('WebSocket connection to wss://…/graphql failed'). The backend now asks the agent to open the socket to the miner (webui_ws_open, with the page's sub-protocol, the miner's own session cookie and Origin http://<miner-ip>), accepts the browser's socket only once the miner has answered, and relays frames both ways (text and binary). Up to 30 live sockets per agent; all are closed if the agent's connection to the backend drops. A socket on another port of the miner (Goldshell's :443 pool-test socket) keeps that port.

Fix Braiins OS 26.x miners not staying logged in through the web UI tunnel: the password was accepted, then the login page came straight back. The agent passed only Content-Type to the miner and returned only Content-Type/Location, so the miner's session cookie (set on /graphql login) never reached the browser and was never sent back, and any Authorization header the miner's own page added was overwritten by the agent's root/root login. The page's Cookie, Accept and Authorization headers are now forwarded to the miner (root/root is only used when the page sends none), and the miner's Set-Cookie is returned to the backend, which scopes it to that miner's tunnel folder.

Fix the ElphaPEX at 19.3.19.46 (and any HTTP-only miner) showing offline with no hashrate while every other field was filled in: its web server answers only one connection at a time, but each poll fired summary.cgi (hashrate), stats.cgi, pools.cgi and the hardware-ID cascade (up to 8 more requests, mostly other brands' endpoints) at it simultaneously. Model, worker, pool, MAC and serial are kept from any cycle that got through, so they filled in over time, but hashrate must arrive in the current cycle and summary.cgi kept losing the race - hashrate 0, status offline. HTTP-only units are now read one request at a time: hashrate first (with one retry), then temp/fan, then pools; hardware IDs only until found, then re-checked every 30 minutes. Machines with the cgminer port (Antminer, Avalon, etc.) are polled exactly as before.

Avalon (Canaan) support for machine locate and control, using the exact commands from Canaan's own management tool (Canaan Mine Master 2.0): LED on/off to find a machine on the rack (ascset|0,led,1-1 / 1-0, sent as plain text to port 4028 the way Canaan does it — the old LED action only knew Antminer's blink.cgi, so it silently did nothing on an Avalon), a real Avalon reboot (ascset|0,reboot,1 — cgminer 'restart' only restarts the mining software), work mode Normal/High Performance (0,workmode,N, optionally rebooting to apply) and fan speed (0,fan-spd,N, 30-100% or -1 for automatic; anything lower is refused so a machine can't be cooked by a typo). An LED switched on to locate a machine now turns itself off again after a set time (default 10 minutes) so forgotten LEDs don't stay lit.

Fix the ElphaPEX at 19.3.19.46 showing hashrate in the wrong unit (0.13 TH/s instead of ~130 GH/s-scale — actually its true ~10-14 GH/s displayed 1000x too small) and the wrong algo badge (SHA-256 instead of Scrypt): getAlgo() never recognized ElphaPEX's own 'DG1+' naming at all (only matched 'l' immediately followed by a digit, which 'dg1+' doesn't contain), so it silently fell through to the SHA-256 default — and that wrong algo is exactly what decides whether hashrate is displayed in GH/s or TH/s. Also now reads temp and fan from this unit's own /cgi-bin/stats.cgi (confirmed: chain[].temp_chip in millidegrees, fan[] in RPM with one slot known to report a bogus value that's now sanity-range-checked out), since — same as hashrate before this — the cgminer TCP path those were read from is never answered by this firmware at all.

Root-caused the ElphaPEX at 19.3.19.46 still showing offline with no hashrate despite model/brand/worker now being correctly detected: this firmware never answers the cgminer TCP port, so the ONLY hashrate source in the code was scraping a 'hashrate by nonce is: X Mhash/s' phrase out of the boot log — and a machine with hashrate stuck at 0 gets forced to status:'offline' regardless of how well everything else was identified. Confirmed directly against this unit's own /cgi-bin/summary.cgi and /cgi-bin/stats.cgi (fetched over plain HTTP, same lowercase-field pattern as pools.cgi) that it reports rate_5s/rate_avg in MH/s there — now read as the primary hashrate source, with the boot-log scrape kept only as a last-resort fallback. Also removed the now-resolved [EP-DEBUG2] diagnostic logging.

Fix the ElphaPEX at 19.3.19.46 (and any other HTTP-only, one-connection-at-a-time unit) showing up in a manual 'Scan Network' but never in the recurring 30s poll: v1.1.32's isAsic() re-verification, needed to stop routers/cameras/printers being swept in as miners, ran its full up-to-6-request signature check against a port-80 device EVERY cycle, forever. Piling those extra probes in front of the one request that actually matters was enough to starve it out on a server that can only handle one connection at a time — confirmed true of at least this ElphaPEX — so the recurring poll kept losing the race that an isolated one-off scan usually won by luck. A unit that already passed isAsic() is now trusted for 10 minutes before being re-checked, so routine cycles skip straight to the real data pull; a device that changes identity (e.g. a router taking over an old miner's IP via DHCP) still gets caught within that same window rather than being trusted forever.

Fix a regression from v1.1.31: widening the recurring poll to also accept port 80 (needed for the ElphaPEX, which doesn't run the cgminer TCP service at all) had no verification step, so literally any device answering on port 80 — a router, a camera, a printer — got swept in and treated as a miner. isAsic() (the same real signature check the manual 'Scan Network' already used) now gates the port-80 case; a port-4028 hit is still accepted directly since that's already a reliable enough signal on its own. Also taught isAsic() to recognize ElphaPEX's own /cgi-bin/pools.cgi signature, since it previously matched none of the existing cgminer/Antminer/Avalon/Whatsminer checks and would have been wrongly rejected by this same verification step.

Found why the v1.1.29 pools.cgi fix never took effect: the recurring 30s poll only ever considered a unit for polling if it answered the cgminer TCP port (4028) within 1.5s — a unit whose firmware doesn't run that service at all (confirmed: 19.3.19.46 was simply never appearing in the agent's own console output, cycle after cycle) was silently skipped before getMinerInfo() — and every one of its HTTP fallbacks — ever ran. It only ever got added to the fleet via a one-off manual 'Scan Network', whose own reachability check already accepted HTTP (port 80) too; the recurring poll now does the same, so an HTTP-only unit keeps getting refreshed every cycle instead of silently going stale after its first scan.

The v1.1.29 fix for ElphaPEX at 19.3.19.46 isn't showing up on the Workers page despite matching the raw pools.cgi JSON — temporarily logs '[EP-DEBUG2]' lines pinned to that exact IP (unconditional, not gated by brand this time) showing httpPools, the TCP pools response, the resolved active pool, and the final worker/model/brand values, so the actual break point can be read off the console. Remove once root-caused.

Root-caused the ElphaPEX blank worker/pool/model fields, confirmed against this exact firmware's own /cgi-bin/pools.cgi response: it uses entirely lowercase field names (user/url/status/priority) instead of stock cgminer's capitalized ones (User/URL/Status/Priority), so every read of those fields was silently matching nothing. All pool/worker reads now check both casings. Also now reads the model and serial number directly from pools.cgi's structured 'INFO' block ({"type":"DG1+","dev_sn":"..."}) as a cleaner, more reliable source than scraping the boot log for them, and falls back to pools.cgi entirely for pool data on units where the cgminer TCP port doesn't return it at all.

Fix the single-instance lock refusing to ever start: it only checked whether SOME process currently has the old PID number, not whether that process is actually the agent. After a crash or a PC reboot, Windows/Node quickly reassigns that same PID to an unrelated process, so the check kept reporting a false 'already running' forever and the agent never started — exactly what happened on the Ghummadh site PC (stuck in a restart loop, never actually polling any miner). The lock file's own last-touched time is now checked too: a genuinely running agent refreshes it every 8s, so anything older than 3 minutes is treated as abandoned and reclaimed, regardless of what process now happens to hold that PID.

Fix ElphaPEX (DG1/DG1+) hashrate and model showing blank/offline: the boot-log read those values depend on was only ever fetched when a machine's MAC and serial number were BOTH still unknown, so a unit that had already been identified some other way silently never got its hashrate parsed at all. The log is now read directly whenever hashrate comes back empty, regardless of why.

Refuse to start when another agent is already running on this PC. Two agents sharing a FARM_ID knock each other off the backend in a loop — one farm was reconnecting every 3.6 seconds, 104 times in six minutes
Back off for five minutes, with a clear explanation, when the backend reports that another agent already holds this FARM_ID, instead of reconnecting immediately and resuming the tug-of-war
Release the instance lock cleanly on exit, and ignore a stale lock left behind by a crashed agent
